findings.title: Rebalanced strategy reuses an irreversibly shut-down queue pool
findings.body: The factory creates FixedQueuePool once during construction, while SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() shuts that pool down. Arroyo creates a new strategy from the same factory when partitions are revoked and reassigned, so the new strategy receives workers that have exited and queues on which shutdown() has already been called. Subsequent queue.put() calls raise queue.ShutDown; SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit() catches that exception and marks the offset complete, allowing messages to be committed without being processed. A normal Kafka rebalance can therefore cause silent data loss until the process is restarted.

findings.title: Failed work items are marked complete and their offsets are committed
findings.body: OrderedQueueWorker.run() logs an exception from result_processor but unconditionally calls complete_offset() in the finally block. The commit loop can consequently commit the offset for a result that was never successfully handled, contradicting the strategy's stated guarantee that offsets are committed only after successful processing and causing failed uptime results to be lost rather than redelivered.

findings.title: Unbounded queues provide no Arroyo backpressure
findings.body: Each work queue is created with queue.Queue() and therefore has no maximum size, and submit() never raises MessageRejected or otherwise blocks. If workers process more slowly than Kafka delivers, Arroyo can continue submitting messages indefinitely, growing memory use and hiding the backlog from Kafka flow control. This also makes the class documentation's claim of natural backpressure when queues fill up incorrect because these queues never fill.

findings.title: Close stops offset committing before workers finish and shutdown drops queued work
findings.body: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close() stops and joins the commit thread before shutting down the queue pool, so results completed by workers afterward have no commit loop left to commit their offsets and will be redelivered. In addition, FixedQueuePool.shutdown() sets each worker's shutdown flag before calling queue.shutdown(immediate=False); a busy worker exits after its current item instead of draining its queue. Graceful close therefore both leaves processed offsets uncommitted and abandons queued work rather than finishing it within the strategy's join period.

findings.title: Python's salted hash does not provide consistent group-to-queue assignment
findings.body: get_queue_for_group() uses the built-in hash() for a string group key. Python randomizes string hashing per interpreter unless PYTHONHASHSEED is fixed, so the same subscription can map to different queues after a restart or when processed by another consumer process. That undermines the documented consistent-assignment and per-group ordering guarantee across rebalances and deployments; a stable digest such as hashlib.md5 or sha256 should be used instead.

findings.title: Invalid max_workers values are silently accepted for thread-queue-parallel mode
findings.body: The CLI accepts any integer for --max-workers, and this code converts 0 to 20 with 'or' while passing a negative value through as num_queues. A negative value creates no queues or workers; submissions then fail with an index/modulo error, are caught by SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit(), and are marked complete, so their offsets can be committed without processing. The option should be validated as a positive integer before constructing the pool.

findings.title: Blocked offsets make commit checks repeatedly scan an ever-growing set
findings.body: OffsetTracker retains every offset after a blocked or very slow offset, because offsets can only be removed after a contiguous commit. get_committable_offsets() is called once per second and computes both min() and max() over that retained set each time. During exactly the slow-item backlog this feature is meant to tolerate, the set can grow to a large number of completed offsets and the commit loop becomes repeated O(n) work while also retaining unbounded tracking state.
